title: Direct-Mapped Cache
constraints: 8 lines of one byte each. `index = addr[2:0]`, `tag = addr[7:3]`. Each line has a valid bit, a 5-bit tag and a data byte. At most one of `rd`, `wr`, `fill`, `inv` is 1 per cycle.

**Lookup** (`rd` or `wr`): hit = the line at `index` is valid and its tag matches. The result is **registered**: after the edge, `hit` holds the lookup result and `rdata` the line's data (don't-care on a miss). On any edge without a lookup, `hit <= 0`.
`wr` is write-through with **no write-allocate**: on a hit the line's data becomes `wdata`. A write miss leaves the cache unchanged.

`fill` installs `fill_data` for `addr` (valid, tag, data) at `index`, replacing whatever was there. `inv` clears every valid bit. `hits` / `misses` count `rd` lookups only (8-bit, wrapping). Synchronous reset clears valid bits, counters and `hit`.
hints: Store `valid[8]`, `tag[8]` and `data[8]` arrays, and compare the tag in the same cycle, before the edge.
Register the compare result: `hit <= lookup && valid[idx] && tag[idx] == addr[7:3]`.
Don't forget that two addresses with the same index (e.g. 0x05 and 0x0D) evict each other: conflict misses.

examples.check: cold miss then fill then hit
examples.title: compulsory miss
examples.expected: miss, then hit with the filled data
